latest_lesson.topic_title: Navigating Office Small Talk and Networking
latest_lesson.article: In today’s fast-paced work environment, mastering the art of small talk is just as important as meeting deadlines. Many employees feel nervous when they have to chat with colleagues or clients near the coffee machine. However, if you want to build strong professional relationships, you need to step out of your comfort zone. For instance, instead of just talking about the weather, try asking open-ended questions like, 'How has your week been so far?' or 'Are you working on anything exciting lately?' Not only does this show genuine interest, but it also helps you find common ground. Furthermore, never underestimate the power of networking events. Even if you are an introvert, setting a small goal, such as meeting two new people, can make a big difference. Remember, rarely does a great opportunity come to those who stay silent in the corner. Should you find yourself feeling anxious, just take a deep breath and keep it simple. By practicing these small interactions daily, you will soon find that professional networking becomes second nature. It is not about being the loudest person in the room; it is about making meaningful connections that last.

vocabulary.meaning_zh: 開放式的（指無法用是或否回答的問題）
vocabulary.example: Using open-ended questions helps to keep the conversation going.
We found some common ground regarding our interest in international travel.
Never underestimate the importance of good communication skills in the workplace.
After months of practice, driving in the city became second nature to me.

vocabulary.meaning_zh: 很少、幾乎不（用於句首時需倒裝）
vocabulary.example: Rarely do I have time to relax during the busy season.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Hey Maya, I read this interesting article about small talk in the office. Do you find it easy to chat with coworkers?

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: To be honest, Alex, not really! Sometimes I just feel awkward standing by the coffee machine.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: I totally get that. The article suggests asking open-ended questions. Like, instead of saying 'It's cold today,' ask 'What are you working on?'

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: That’s a great point. It makes the conversation feel more natural, right?

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Exactly. And it helps you find common ground with people you don't know well.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: True. But what about networking events? I usually end up hiding in the corner.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Haha, I’ve been there! The trick is to set small goals, like just talking to two new people.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: That sounds much more manageable. I’ll definitely try that next time.

comprehension_quiz.question: What does the author suggest to improve professional networking?
options: Focusing only on technical work deadlines.
Asking open-ended questions to find common ground.
Avoiding networking events to stay comfortable.
Talking about the weather as much as possible.
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 文章中提到為了建立專業關係，應使用開放式問題來尋找共同點，而非僅談論天氣。

comprehension_quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence structure: 'Rarely ___ a great opportunity come to those who stay silent.'
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 當否定副詞 Rarely 放在句首時，句子需要倒裝。主詞 'a great opportunity' 是單數，因此助動詞使用 does。
